fields.meta_description: Build a Facebook ads landing page for a carousel ad, a local quote, a webinar or a headline test, with every lead saved. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Facebook Ads Landing Page That Saves Every Lead
fields.hero_description: Build a Facebook ads landing page that matches your ad and saves every lead to a database you own.
fields.explore_cta: Build My Facebook Ads Landing Page
fields.features_heading: What Happens Between the Ad and the Lead
fields.features_subheading: The ad wins the tap. Emergent builds what the tap opens: a page that repeats the ad's offer, and a table of every lead it brings.
fields.feature_1:
One page per ad, built from a prompt

Paste the ad's headline and offer, and Emergent builds a page that opens on the same words, with a short form and a leads table. A second ad with a new angle takes one more prompt.
fields.feature_2:
The ad's tag saved on each lead

Add URL parameters to the link in your ad, and the page reads them when it loads. Each lead is saved with the campaign and ad names it arrived with, next to the answers given.
fields.feature_3:
Leads in a database you own

Every form submission lands as a row in a database you own, with the time and the answers. Sort the rows by ad, or send new ones to a CRM such as HubSpot through its API.
fields.feature_4:
An email for the lead a person should call

Set a rule, such as a quote request from a ZIP code you serve, and the app emails that lead to the person who handles it. Leads outside the rule wait in the table for a weekly read.
fields.feature_5:
A second headline, by prompt

Ask for another version of the page with a new headline, and Emergent builds it at its own link. Point one ad at each version, then count each version's requests in the table.
fields.feature_6:
Your page as code, or hosted

Export the page and its leads table to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Or keep it hosted on Emergent at your own domain (custom domains use credits) and change it by prompt.

fields.tab_content_1:
Half the sample requests came from the wool card

Loomhaven Rugs runs one carousel ad with three cards, wool, jute and cotton, and each card's link opens its own section of one sample request page. Every request is saved with the card's tag. Of last month's 300 requests, the wool card brought 150, jute 90, and cotton 60.
fields.tab_content_2:
Any quote inside 14 ZIP codes reaches Ossian Marr

Homeowners who tap Cobalt Peak Roofing's ad get a quote page that asks for a ZIP code and the roof type. A request from one of the 14 ZIP codes the company serves is emailed to its estimator, Ossian Marr. Anyone else is told the area is not served yet. Each request is saved to the quotes table.
fields.tab_content_3:
238 registrants, reminded 1 hour before the start

Tallyfern sells bookkeeping software and runs an ad for a free 45-minute webinar on closing the month. The registration page asks for a name and a work email, then emails each registrant a calendar link at once. A reminder follows 1 hour before the start. The ad brought 238 registrants.
fields.tab_content_4:
On 1,000 visits each, the prep headline won 61 to 38

Sprigwell Kitchen wrote two headlines for its meal kit trial box, one about price and one about skipping Sunday prep, and built a version of the page for each. Two ads point to the two versions, and each link carries its own tag. After 1,000 visits each, the prep page had 61 trial requests and the price page 38.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Facebook Ads Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan a Facebook ads landing page around one ad, test it on a phone, and trace each lead to its ad.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide what the ad asks people to do
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Open the page on the ad's own words
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask only for the fields you will use
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Tag the ad's link with URL parameters
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pick the one action the ad asks for: request a sample, get a quote, register, or start a trial. The page asks for that action alone. A visitor who taps an ad about a rug sample should not land on your full catalog.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Repeat the headline and offer the ad already made, in the same words, and use the ad's image or a close match above the form. When the page changes the promise, the visitor has to work out whether they landed in the right place.
fields.howto_step_3_des: List what you need to act on the lead, such as a ZIP code for a quote or a work email for a webinar, and cut the rest. Each extra field is one more thing a person types on a phone keyboard.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Add URL parameters to the destination link in Ads Manager, such as the campaign and ad names. Meta's Business Help Center says you can use them to identify where your ad traffic is coming from and which ads helped drive a conversion.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Add the Meta Pixel to the page
fields.howto_step_5_des: Install the Meta Pixel on the page before the ad goes live if you want reports past the click. Meta tracks landing page views when people use its in-app browser or when a Meta Pixel is installed on the page itself.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Test it from the ad preview
fields.howto_step_6_des: Preview the ad on a phone and tap through to the page, as a visitor would. Check that the headline shows before any scrolling, the form opens the right keyboard for email and ZIP code, and a test lead lands in the table with its tag.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Describe the ad and its offer, and Emergent builds the page and the table its leads land in. Ask for changes by prompt, such as a second headline to test. The free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: What is the difference between landing page views and link clicks in Facebook ads?
faq_plan.ref: What is the difference between landing page views and link clicks in Facebook ads?

prov.original: What is the difference between landing page views and link clicks in Facebook ads?

faq_plan.a: A link click counts the tap on your ad's link, and a landing page view counts the page loading after that tap. Meta says you can compare the two to see how many times people may have clicked on your ad but left before the website loaded. A wide gap is a reason to check how your Facebook ads landing page loads on a phone.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a Facebook ads landing page?
faq_plan.a: Start from the ad: note its headline and the one action it asks for, then build a page that repeats both. With Emergent's AI landing page builder, you describe that page in a prompt, and Emergent builds it with its form and a leads table. Keep the page to that one action.

faq_plan.q: What should a Facebook ad landing page show before anyone scrolls?
faq_plan.a: Four things, on a phone screen: the headline the ad used, one line on the offer, the form or its first field, and the button. Leave the menu and other offers off the page. Each one is a way out of a visit the ad already paid for.

faq_plan.q: Can a Facebook ads landing page promote an affiliate offer?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Build the page on your own domain, put a plain disclosure near the top, and send each button to the merchant through your tracked link. An affiliate landing page set up this way keeps the ad's URL parameters with each visit, so you can see which ad sent each click before the merchant's report arrives.

faq_plan.q: What can a Facebook ads landing page do that a lead form ad cannot?
faq_plan.a: It gives you room for the full offer and runs rules on the answers, such as a ZIP code check that decides who gets the quote. Meta's Business Help Center says instant forms can help you generate and qualify leads by asking people to fill out a form. Choose your own page when the follow-up depends on what people answer.

faq_plan.q: How does a Facebook ads landing page show which ad sent each lead?
faq_plan.a: It reads the URL parameters on each ad's link and saves them with the lead. Give each ad its own parameters, such as a campaign name and an ad name. Each row in the leads table then carries its ad, so you can count leads per ad in one place. Emergent builds the page to read those parameters and write them to a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Does a Facebook ads landing page need SEO?
faq_plan.a: Not for the ad traffic: those visitors arrive from the ad, not from search. If the page should also be found in search, give it a real title and text a search engine can read. Basic landing page seo matters more for an offer that runs all year than for a three-week campaign.

faq_plan.q: Should each Facebook ad get its own landing page?
faq_plan.a: Give an ad its own page when it promises something the others do not, such as a different product or headline. Ads that make the same promise can share one landing page, and Facebook ads that link to it with their own URL parameters still show which one sent each lead. A carousel ad can go further, with a different destination URL for each card.

faq_plan.q: What should I test first on a Facebook ads landing page?
faq_plan.a: Test the headline first, since it is the line that has to match the ad. Build a second version of the page with the new headline, send one ad to each version, and tag each link. Once both have a similar number of visits, compare leads per visit and keep the winner. In Emergent, the second version takes one prompt.

faq_plan.q: Can a Facebook ads landing page double as the link in a profile bio?
faq_plan.a: It can, but the two visitors want different things. An ad visitor tapped one offer, while a bio visitor is browsing a profile and expects a menu of links. Build the bio its own page, such as an instagram landing page with a button per offer. Emergent builds both pages, and their leads land in one database you own.

Each tab follows the click to the row it leaves in a database the advertiser owns.
